classification.difficultyReason: Translate the intercept and tangent point into two value equations, use the horizontal tangent to form a derivative equation, then solve the three conditions together.

content.prompt: The graph of $y=ax^2+bx+c$ has an $x$-intercept at $x=-2$. The tangent at $(1,-18)$ is horizontal. Find the values of $a$, $b$, and $c$.

answer.worked:
Substitute the points $(-2,0)$ and $(1,-18)$ into the equation of the graph.

$$\begin{align*}4a-2b+c&=0\\a+b+c&=-18\end{align*}$$

The horizontal tangent gives $y'=0$ at $x=1$.

$$\begin{align*}y'&=2ax+b\\2a+b&=0\\b&=-2a\end{align*}$$

Substituting $b=-2a$ into $a+b+c=-18$ gives $c=a-18$. Substitute both expressions into the intercept equation.

$$\begin{align*}4a-2(-2a)+(a-18)&=0\\9a-18&=0\\a&=2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}b&=-2(2)=-4\\c&=2-18=-16\end{align*}$$
